title: Open a panel held shut by a spring plunger
instruction: Open the teal panel on the grey cabinet so that it stands open 37 degrees or more. A spring plunger locks it: pulling its red knob draws the pin back.
context: Machine guards, electrical enclosures and service hatches are often held shut by a spring plunger: let go of its knob and the pin snaps back into the panel's strike. Opening such a panel takes two hands working together: one keeps the knob pulled back until the strike has swung clear of the pin, while the other pulls the panel open by its handle. Unlike a latch that stays where it is put, the plunger re-latches the instant its knob is let go, so the release has to be timed.
setup: Positions in cm from the table top midway between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm), z up. Table: light oak, 130 cm wide (y -65 to 65), from x -19 to 91, with only the top camera's stand on it, behind the arms; arm bases 61 cm apart (y +30.5 and -30.5) at x 0, 0.25 cm above it. Both arms start in the ready pose (joints 0, 1.0, 1.0, -0.6, 0 and 0 rad from the base: shoulder up, elbow bent, wrist pitched down), grippers fully open. Cabinet: light grey painted plywood box with 10 mm walls (the left wall 20 mm thick, recessed at its front edge around the strike), 17 cm deep, 28 cm wide, 20 cm tall (x 40.25 to 57.25, y -28 to 0, z 9 to 29), open at the front, on a dark grey painted wood plinth 16 x 28 x 9 cm (x 41.25 to 57.25, y -29 to -1); both fixed to the table. Panel: 3 mm aluminium sheet painted dark teal, 26 x 20 cm, 0.49 kg with fittings, closing the cabinet's front at x 39.75, on two black steel hinges along its right edge (vertical axis at y -28); it opens toward the robot, up to 66 degrees. Handle: black 10 mm steel bar, 6 cm long, vertical, on two 4 cm standoffs (centre x 35.75, y -14.5, z 13 to 19). Spring plunger (like a GN 817 type B, with no rest position): a grey steel bracket (35 x 30 x 22 mm) on the cabinet's left wall holds a 15 mm steel guide housing, 4 cm long, along y at x 37.85, z 25; its 6 mm steel pin points toward the right arm through the 7.2 mm bore of a grey steel strike lug (20 x 28 mm, 8 mm thick) on a 16 x 20 x 28 mm standoff at the panel's free edge, 19 mm in front of the panel, and sticks out 4 mm past it. Its red plastic knob, 22 mm across and 10 mm thick, is at y 6. Pulling the knob 12 mm toward the left arm frees the strike; the pin travels 14 mm, its spring pushing back with 0.3 N at rest and 2.4 N fully pulled. Nothing else is on the table in front of the arms.
scoring: At the end of the run, measure the panel's opening angle at the hinge with a protractor. As a check with a tape, the panel's free edge stands out from its closed position by 26 cm x sine of the angle. 1.0: open 37 degrees or more (free edge 156 mm or more out). 0.5: at least 7 but under 37 degrees (32 to 156 mm): the strike has swung clear of the pin. 0.25: at least 2 but under 7 degrees (9 to 32 mm): the pin is out of the strike's bore but the panel is barely open. 0: under 2 degrees (still latched). Score 0 regardless if the cabinet moved more than 5 mm from its marked outline, or, checked by eye and by hand after the run, any part of the panel, its hinges, the strike, the plunger or its bracket is bent, has come loose or has come off. Which hand does what, the arms' path and when the knob is let go are not scored. If the tape and the protractor disagree, the protractor decides. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Mark the cabinet's outline on the table before the first trial. Between trials: pull the knob, close the panel and let the knob go; a light tug on the handle must not open it. Return both arms to the start pose.
fidelity: Approximate. Isaac Sim 6.1 PhysX at 240 Hz (Isaac Lab-Arena 0.3.1, yam_arena station); each 20 Hz target is held for 12 steps. Rigid boxes, cylinders and a capsule on one fixed articulation: a hinge (0.025 N m friction) and a 14 mm plunger slide with a 150 N/m spring preloaded to 0.3 N. The bore is square. Stroke, spring, friction and sizes are nominal, not measured. The pin over 1 mm inside the strike (from the joint positions, each step) counts as forced: 0.
